resources.string: A lightweight, pure Android call forwarding and screening tool based on carrier rules

▪ Targeted Forwarding List: Precisely screen specific contacts/numbers without affecting regular calls.
▪ Flexible Adding: Add manually, load from contacts, or load from recent call logs.
▪ Time Window Control: Configure active time ranges, including overnight windows (e.g. 22:00 ~ 07:00).
▪ History & Export: Record each screened call with date/time details and support history export.
▪ Lightweight: No background battery drain, no tracking SDKs, privacy-focused.

1. Enable Carrier Busy Forwarding: Configure busy forwarding in your phone's dialer settings or via common USSD codes:
 • Enable: Dial **67*DestinationNumber#
 • Cancel: Dial ##67#
 • Query: Dial *#67#

2. Permissions Required: Grant "Default Call Screening App" role and "Contacts" permission on first launch so screening and contact matching work properly.

In daily life, we often encounter calls that we do not want to answer but cannot bluntly decline, or calls we wish to delegate during meetings or rest. iForward is lightweight, free of permanent background daemons, ad-free, and open source. It combines modern Android CallScreeningService with carrier-side call forwarding to achieve seamless forwarding and realistic screening.
This project is completely free and open source.\nSpecial thanks to the original author Hanley and early contributors for their support.
Sometimes we do not want to answer the phone and cannot hang up either. iForward leverages Android call screening and carrier busy forwarding to achieve realistic screening and call forwarding.
